question_or_title: What is the NIN and who issues it?
answer_or_content: The National Identification Number (NIN) is an 11-digit number assigned to every individual enrolled in Nigeria's National Identity Database (NIDB), managed by the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC). It ties together all official records about a person and is required for SIM registration, bank accounts, passports, exams, and most government services. All citizens and legal residents, from birth, are eligible to enrol.

question_or_title: Can I complete NIN registration fully online?
answer_or_content: No. Full NIN registration cannot be completed entirely online. You can pre-enrol online at the NIMC pre-enrolment portal (penrol.nimc.gov.ng), which generates a barcoded slip, but you must still visit an approved NIMC enrolment centre in person to complete biometric capture (ten fingerprints, facial photo, and signature) before a NIN is issued.

question_or_title: How do I pre-enrol for a NIN online?
answer_or_content: Visit the NIMC pre-enrolment portal at penrol.nimc.gov.ng, click 'Pre-Enrolment Portal', and complete the online form with your personal details. This generates a pre-enrolment slip with a barcode. Take the printed slip to an approved NIMC enrolment centre, where an officer scans the barcode to populate your details, lets you verify them, then captures your fingerprints and facial image. A Transaction ID Slip is issued as proof, and the NIN follows after processing.

question_or_title: What is the NIMC Ward-Level Enrolment Drive?
answer_or_content: Starting 16 February 2026, NIMC launched a nationwide Ward-Level Enrolment Drive to decentralise NIN registration, setting up enrolment points closer to communities so citizens (including students) do not have to travel far to register. Nigerians can find their nearest ward centre via NIMC's official channels or the toll-free line.

question_or_title: Is NIN mandatory for SSCE (WAEC/NECO) candidates?
answer_or_content: Yes. NIMC has stated that NIN is required for the Senior Secondary School Certificate Examinations, as well as for school registrations and scholarship applications. Students under 16 must be accompanied to the registration centre by a parent or guardian who has a valid NIN, and should bring the child's original birth certificate or a statutory declaration of age.

question_or_title: How do I modify or correct my NIN details?
answer_or_content: Data modifications (such as name, date of birth, or address corrections) are handled through NIMC's official self-service modification portal at selfservicemodification.nimc.gov.ng. NIMC has warned Nigerians against using unauthorized third-party websites for this, since it can expose personal data to fraud; only the official portal should be used.

question_or_title: How can I register for a NIN while living outside Nigeria?
answer_or_content: To register for a NIN from abroad, visit the official NIMC website to locate a licensed diaspora enrolment partner in your country of residence, book an appointment, and attend with valid documents such as a Nigerian passport or birth certificate. Your biometrics will be captured at that partner centre and a NIN issued after processing.

question_or_title: What app can I use to access my NIN digitally?
answer_or_content: The NIMC Mobile ID app (available on iOS and Android) lets a user retrieve and display their digital NIN by entering their 11-digit NIN number, after which it can be used as a form of ID verification without carrying the physical slip or card. NIMC also runs a separate NINAUTH app for digital identity authentication services.

question_or_title: How many Nigerians had been enrolled in the NIN database as of late 2025?
answer_or_content: NIMC disclosed that enrolment in the National Identification Number database had reached approximately 127 million as of December 2025, with enrolment figures fairly balanced between the northern and southern regions of the country.

question_or_title: Does NYSC verify my full NIN record during registration?
answer_or_content: No. During NYSC online registration, applicants enter their NIN at the biodata stage, but NYSC only uses it to verify the applicant's name against NIMC's database. It does not fetch date of birth, gender, state of origin, or other personal details. Applicants should ensure the name on their NIN exactly matches what is on their university/NYSC senate list to avoid rejection.

question_or_title: How much does a Nigerian international passport cost in 2026 (applying within Nigeria)?
answer_or_content: As of 2026, applications made within Nigeria cost ₦100,000 for the 32-page booklet (5-year validity) and ₦200,000 for the 64-page booklet (10-year validity). These fees took effect 1 September 2025, roughly doubling the prior (August 2024) rates. Renewal costs the same as a fresh passport; there is no discounted renewal rate.

question_or_title: How much does a Nigerian passport cost for applicants abroad (diaspora)?
answer_or_content: For Nigerians applying from outside the country, the fee is unchanged from prior years at $150 for the 32-page (5-year) passport and $230 for the 64-page (10-year) passport, paid via the NIS online portal, regardless of the naira fee increase that applies to domestic applications.

question_or_title: What is the step-by-step process to apply for a Nigerian passport online?
answer_or_content: Visit passport.immigration.gov.ng, create an account, and complete the application form. Select your preferred passport office (or embassy, if abroad) for biometric capture. Pay the passport fee online through the NIS portal and keep the receipt/reference number. Book a biometric capture appointment and attend in person with required documents (fingerprints and photograph are captured there). Track your application status online using your reference number and date of birth; you'll be notified when the passport is ready for collection.

question_or_title: How long does it take to get a Nigerian passport in 2026?
answer_or_content: As of January 2026, official timelines after biometric capture are about 3 weeks for renewals and roughly 6 weeks for fresh applications. The Minister of Interior has indicated some optimized cases can be ready within one week via the Automated Passport Application Process.

question_or_title: Do I need a NIN to get a Nigerian passport?
answer_or_content: Yes. Applicants (including those abroad) need a National Identification Number issued by NIMC before completing a passport application; those abroad without one should enrol for NIN at a Nigerian embassy offering NIN services if available in their country.

question_or_title: What should I do if there's an error in my passport data?
answer_or_content: Passport data is printed exactly as it exists in the NIMC (NIN) database, so any data error must first be corrected at NIMC level via the self-service modification portal or a NIMC office — it cannot be fixed directly on the passport application portal.

question_or_title: Can I renew my Nigerian passport contactlessly?
answer_or_content: Yes, for eligible applicants. The NIS Mobile app allows a contactless renewal option where eligible applicants can complete biometrics without visiting a passport office in person, and online renewal (with home delivery in some cases) is available for Nigerians in countries such as Canada, UK, US, and Italy.

question_or_title: How much validity should remain on my passport before I travel?
answer_or_content: Most embassies and airlines require at least six months of remaining passport validity before permitting travel or visa issuance, so applicants are advised to begin renewal 9–12 months before expiry rather than waiting until the passport is close to or past expiry.

question_or_title: 32-page or 64-page: which Nigerian passport should I choose?
answer_or_content: The cost per year of validity is identical for both (₦20,000/year): ₦100,000 for 5 years (32-page) or ₦200,000 for 10 years (64-page). Occasional travellers (1–4 trips/year) are generally better served by the cheaper 32-page 5-year option, while frequent business travellers or those needing many visa stamps benefit from the 64-page 10-year booklet to avoid running out of pages mid-validity.

question_or_title: What is CAC registration and who needs it?
answer_or_content: CAC registration is the legal process of recording a business or organisation with Nigeria's Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC). Anyone operating a business, company, partnership, NGO, church, foundation, club, or association in Nigeria is legally required to register with the CAC. Without registration, you cannot open a corporate bank account, bid for government contracts, or legally protect your business name.

question_or_title: How much does it cost to register a business name with CAC in 2026?
answer_or_content: Business name (sole proprietorship/partnership) registration costs roughly ₦11,000–₦25,000 in official CAC fees as of 2026: about ₦1,000–₦1,200 for name reservation (the CAC portal added a ₦200 'AI service fee' from its Version 3.0 update) plus roughly ₦10,000–₦20,000 for registration itself, depending on when the fee schedule was last updated. Realistic all-in cost including bank portal/Remita charges is typically ₦15,000–₦35,000.

question_or_title: How much does it cost to register a private limited company (LTD) with CAC in 2026?
answer_or_content: For a company with share capital up to ₦1 million, official CAC incorporation fees run roughly ₦30,000–₦40,000, excluding stamp duty and professional/agent fees. For share capital exceeding ₦1 million, the CAC fee increases by about ₦10,000 for every additional ₦1 million of share capital, plus a 0.75% FIRS stamp duty (roughly ₦7,500 per additional ₦1 million).

question_or_title: How long is a CAC name reservation valid?
answer_or_content: A reserved business/company name is held for 60 days from approval. If registration is not completed within that window, the reservation expires and the name-reservation step must be repeated.

question_or_title: What is the CAC annual returns requirement and fee?
answer_or_content: Every CAC-registered entity must file annual returns to keep its status 'Active'. The yearly fee is about ₦3,000 for Business Names and ₦5,000 for Companies. Missing the annual return deadline attracts a monthly late-filing penalty that can quickly exceed the original registration fee.

question_or_title: Can I register a business with CAC entirely online?
answer_or_content: Yes. As of 2026, business registration in Nigeria is handled completely through the CAC online portal — name search and reservation, submission of the registration form with business/owner details, and payment can all be completed online without visiting a CAC office in person.

question_or_title: What documents do I need to register a business name with CAC?
answer_or_content: You typically need: a proposed business name (checked for availability), the nature of the business, the principal business address, and the personal details (including means of ID) of the proprietor(s) or partners. For a sole proprietorship you provide your own details; for a partnership, details of all partners are required.

question_or_title: What is the CAC fee to get a Certified True Copy (CTC) of my registration documents?
answer_or_content: Re-obtaining Certified True Copies of CAC registration documents (for example, if the originals are lost) costs between ₦2,500 and ₦5,000 per document as of 2026.

question_or_title: What replaced the old TIN system in Nigeria from 2026?
answer_or_content: Under the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 (effective 1 January 2026), the previously separate TINs issued by FIRS, the Joint Tax Board, and state tax authorities have been unified into a single 'Tax ID.' TINs issued before 2026 remain valid under the new harmonised system; every 'taxable person' (anyone carrying on trade, business, or economic activity to earn income) must have a Tax ID.

question_or_title: Do I need to separately apply for a Tax ID if my business is CAC-registered?
answer_or_content: Usually not. Under the harmonised system introduced by the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, a business's CAC registration number (RC number for companies, BN number for business names) is automatically linked to its Tax ID, so most CAC-registered businesses already have one without a separate application.

question_or_title: How do I register for a TIN with FIRS?
answer_or_content: Companies incorporated with CAC after 1 September 2023 can self-register for a TIN online via the FIRS TaxPro Max self-registration module. Businesses/companies registered before that date must visit the nearest FIRS office in person with incorporation documents (Memorandum & Articles of Association, Certificate of Incorporation, Form CAC 1.1 status report) to complete registration manually.

question_or_title: How do I register for VAT in Nigeria?
answer_or_content: A Tax Identification Number (TIN) is a prerequisite. Obtain or confirm your TIN online at tin.firs.gov.ng or via etax.firs.gov.ng, then complete VAT registration (duly completed and stamped VAT Form 001) either online through the FIRS portal or at an FIRS office with your business registration documents, TIN, and bank details. Once approved, FIRS issues a VAT Registration Certificate, and your VAT number (your TIN) must appear on every tax invoice thereafter.

question_or_title: What is the VAT rate in Nigeria and when are VAT returns due?
answer_or_content: The standard VAT rate is 7.5%, charged as a separate line item on taxable goods/services invoices — it is not to be blended into the price. VAT returns and payment of the net VAT collected are due by the 21st of the month following the transaction month (for example, March VAT is due by 21 April).

question_or_title: What are Nigeria's 2026 personal income tax (PAYE) bands under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025?
answer_or_content: Effective 1 January 2026: 0% on the first ₦800,000 of annual income (fully tax-free); 15% on the next ₦2.2 million (i.e., ₦800,001–₦3,000,000); 18% on the next ₦9 million (₦3,000,001–₦12,000,000); 21% on the next ₦13 million (₦12,000,001–₦25,000,000); 23% on the next ₦25 million (₦25,000,001–₦50,000,000); and 25% on income above ₦50 million. These are marginal rates applied band by band, not flat rates on total income.

question_or_title: Who is exempt from personal income tax under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025?
answer_or_content: Individuals earning at or below the annual amount equivalent to the national minimum wage, and in general anyone earning ₦800,000 or less per year, are fully exempt from personal income tax under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025's Fourth Schedule and Section 58.

question_or_title: What replaced the Consolidated Relief Allowance (CRA) in the 2026 tax reform?
answer_or_content: The old Consolidated Relief Allowance has been abolished and replaced with a simpler 'rent relief': individuals can deduct 20% of their annual rent paid, up to a maximum of ₦500,000, from taxable income before PAYE is calculated.

question_or_title: What are the four laws that make up Nigeria's 2025/2026 tax reform package?
answer_or_content: The reform package comprises four Acts: the Nigeria Tax Act (NTA), the Nigeria Tax Administration Act (NTAA), the Nigeria Revenue Service (Establishment) Act, and the Joint Revenue Board (Establishment) Act. Together they repeal and replace the former Personal Income Tax Act, Companies Income Tax Act, Value Added Tax Act, Capital Gains Tax Act, Petroleum Profits Tax Act, and Stamp Duties Act.

question_or_title: Has FIRS been renamed under the 2026 tax reforms?
answer_or_content: Yes. FIRS has been reconstituted as the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) under the Nigeria Revenue Service (Establishment) Act, one of the four laws in the 2025 tax reform package that took effect 1 January 2026. Similarly, the Joint Tax Board has been rebranded as the Joint Revenue Board.

question_or_title: What is the Company Income Tax (CIT) exemption threshold for small businesses under the 2025 reform?
answer_or_content: The Nigeria Tax Act 2025 raised the small-company CIT exemption threshold to businesses with annual turnover up to ₦100 million, meaning qualifying small companies pay 0% Company Income Tax, as part of a broader package that also abolished the old minimum tax and raised the Capital Gains Tax exemption threshold to ₦150 million.

question_or_title: What is Nigeria's Capital Gains Tax rate for companies under the 2025 reform?
answer_or_content: The Capital Gains Tax rate for companies was increased from 10% to 30% under the Nigeria Finance Act/Nigeria Tax Act 2025 changes effective from January 2026.

question_or_title: Do employees now need a TIN/Tax ID to be paid through payroll?
answer_or_content: Yes. The Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 requires all taxable persons, including salaried employees, to hold a valid Tax Identification Number. Employers/HR teams are expected to verify TIN compliance for every employee, and employees without a TIN may face restrictions in payroll tax processing.

question_or_title: When is the annual personal income tax return deadline in Nigeria?
answer_or_content: The annual income tax return deadline in Nigeria is 31 March of the year following the tax year (e.g., the 2025 tax year return is due by 31 March 2026).

question_or_title: What is the new withholding tax rate on Treasury Bills and short-term bonds under the 2025 reform?
answer_or_content: The Nigeria Tax Act 2025 introduced a 10% withholding tax on Treasury Bills, commercial paper, and bonds with a maturity of less than one year.

question_or_title: Is registering for tax with FIRS/NRS optional for a new business?
answer_or_content: No. Registering for taxes is a legal obligation, not optional. A new business must register with the tax authority (now Nigeria Revenue Service) and file returns on a self-assessment basis; simply having a CAC number does not by itself mean VAT registration is complete — that is a separate registration step.

question_or_title: How much does a Nigerian driver's licence cost in 2026?
answer_or_content: The official FRSC fee is ₦15,000 for a 3-year licence or ₦21,000 for a 5-year licence. This fee covers the application, biometric capture, learner's permit, and licence card. Realistic all-in costs — including accredited driving school (₦20,000–₦50,000), the learner's permit, and VIO test — typically total ₦45,000–₦82,000 when done independently, or ₦75,000–₦147,000 when using an agent.

question_or_title: What is the process to apply for a new Nigerian driver's licence?
answer_or_content: First complete training at an FRSC-accredited driving school and pass its exit test. Apply online at nigeriadriverslicence.frsc.gov.ng, filling in personal details (name, DOB, address, NIN, phone, blood group, next of kin) and uploading your driving school certificate. Choose an FRSC Drivers Licence Centre (DLC) for biometric capture, generate a payment reference and pay via Remita or a supported bank channel, then print the acknowledgement slip and temporary licence. Visit the chosen DLC in person for fingerprint, photo, and signature capture, and take a road test if it isn't waived. A temporary licence is valid for 60 days while the permanent card is produced.

question_or_title: When can I renew my Nigerian driver's licence?
answer_or_content: A licence holder may apply for renewal at any time from 30 days before the expiry date. The renewal process is completed online (application and payment), followed by a VIO test and a visit to an FRSC Drivers Licence Centre for biometric capture.

question_or_title: How do I register for a Permanent Voter's Card (PVC) online in 2026?
answer_or_content: Go to the INEC Self-Service CVR (Continuous Voter Registration) Portal at cvr.inecnigeria.org/online and select 'Register Online.' You'll need to create an account and verify your National Identification Number (NIN). Online registration uses the INEC mobile application to capture your passport photograph and fingerprints via your smartphone; the portal displays a QR code/link to continue biometric capture on your device. After reviewing your submitted details, you finalize the application through the portal.

question_or_title: What if I don't have a NIN or don't want to do biometric capture on my phone for PVC registration?
answer_or_content: You can choose the 'Pre-Registration' option: complete the online pre-registration form with your biodata, schedule an appointment, print the acknowledgement slip, and visit the selected INEC registration centre in person to complete fingerprint and photograph capture. This shortens the wait at the centre since biodata is already on file.

question_or_title: Who is eligible to register as a voter in Nigeria?
answer_or_content: Every Nigerian citizen aged 18 years or above is entitled to register as a voter, including persons living with any form of disability. Each person must appear in person to register or to collect their PVC — registration or collection by proxy is not allowed and is an offence.

question_or_title: Does a Permanent Voter's Card (PVC) expire?
answer_or_content: No. All Permanent Voter's Cards issued by INEC do not expire.

question_or_title: How do I transfer my voter registration to a new polling unit?
answer_or_content: Registered voters who have moved to a new state, city, or neighbourhood can request a transfer of their polling unit through the INEC CVR portal (cvr.inecnigeria.org) using the 'Start Transfer Request' option, or by visiting an INEC State/Local Government office in person with their registration details.

question_or_title: What documents do I need to collect my PVC?
answer_or_content: Bring a valid means of identification (such as a National ID/NIN slip, international passport, or driver's licence) and your printed application/registration slip from the online registration process. Collection must be done in person at the designated INEC office; PVCs are not issued by proxy.

question_or_title: What is the only document INEC accepts for voter accreditation at elections?
answer_or_content: Under Section 47(1) of the Electoral Act 2022 (as amended), the Permanent Voter's Card (PVC) remains the only valid document for voter accreditation at Nigerian elections.

question_or_title: Which agency issues birth certificates in Nigeria and where do I register?
answer_or_content: The National Population Commission (NPC) is responsible for registering every birth in Nigeria and issuing birth certificates. Registration can be done at NPC Local Government Headquarters, NPC registration posts located in hospitals and health centres, or other designated NPC registration centres nationwide.

question_or_title: How do I register my child's birth online through the NPC self-service portal?
answer_or_content: Visit the NPC birth registration self-service portal at birthreg-selfservice.nationalpopulation.gov.ng, go to 'Services', and select 'Birth Registration (Self Service).' The service is only available for children born in Nigeria who already have a National Identification Number (NIN), and requires that at least one parent is Nigerian and holds a valid birth certificate. After agreeing to the terms, you enter your email and pay a non-refundable ₦2,000 registration fee online to proceed. The certificate can only be downloaded once after a successful application; a separate reprint request is needed for additional copies.

question_or_title: Can an adult (18+) get a birth certificate in Nigeria if one was never issued?
answer_or_content: Historically, NPC guidance has distinguished between minors and adults: individuals under 18 can obtain a standard birth certificate, while adults over 18 without a prior registration typically obtain an 'attestation letter' instead — a legal document backing an Age Declaration Affidavit — through the NPC's late registration process, sometimes requiring a sworn affidavit from a High Court if no hospital birth record exists.

question_or_title: Why might I need to authenticate my Nigerian birth certificate?
answer_or_content: Birth certificate authentication is a certification process by Nigeria's Ministry of Foreign Affairs that validates an NPC-issued birth certificate so it is legally recognized by foreign governments, embassies, and international institutions — typically required for visa applications, immigration, or legal proceedings abroad. The Ministry verifies the document originated from the NPC, that signatures/seals are genuine, and that the content hasn't been altered.

question_or_title: Why does NIMC say a NIN requires a birth certificate first?
answer_or_content: For children, NIMC enrolment for a NIN requires either an original birth certificate or a statutory declaration of age. Where a child's birth was never registered, parents must first go through the NPC's late registration process to obtain a birth certificate or age declaration before the child can be enrolled for a NIN — a step now especially relevant since NIN is required for 2026 WAEC/NECO registration.

question_or_title: What is a Tax Clearance Certificate (TCC) and who issues it?
answer_or_content: A Tax Clearance Certificate (TCC) is an official document certifying that an individual or company has settled its tax liabilities, typically covering the three years immediately preceding the current assessment year. For companies it is issued by the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS, formerly FIRS); for individuals it is issued by the relevant State Internal Revenue Service (SIRS), or FIRS/NRS directly for those resident in the FCT.

question_or_title: What is a TCC commonly required for?
answer_or_content: A TCC is commonly required for: bidding on government contracts, obtaining credit facilities/loans from Nigerian banks, visa applications (many foreign embassies require it), import/export licences, registering or transferring ownership of property, and company incorporation or directorship filings.

question_or_title: How do existing companies obtain a TCC online in 2026?
answer_or_content: For existing companies (registered for tax and having filed corporate tax returns for two or more years), the process is fully automated: log in to the E-Services TCC portal at tcc.firs.gov.ng, click 'Generate TCC', and — provided your returns are up to date and taxes paid — a copy is sent to your registered email address, sometimes instantly.

question_or_title: What is the general step-by-step process to obtain a TCC?
answer_or_content: 1) Ensure you have a valid Tax ID/TIN. 2) File all outstanding personal/company income tax returns for the past three years with the relevant tax authority (SIRS for individuals, NRS/FIRS for companies or FCT residents). 3) Pay any outstanding taxes, penalties, and interest. 4) Submit the TCC application online (or in person) with supporting documents such as incorporation documents and bank statements. 5) The tax authority reviews compliance and issues the TCC, valid for one year from the date of issue.

question_or_title: Can Lagos residents generate an electronic TCC (eTCC) instantly?
answer_or_content: Yes, if their records are complete. Through the LIRS e-Tax portal (etax.lirs.net), an eligible taxpayer files outstanding Personal Income Tax returns, ensures their employer has filed matching PAYE returns, updates their profile with a recent passport photo and address, pays any outstanding assessments, and can then generate an eTCC instantly, complete with QR code and certificate number.

question_or_title: What is a Certificate of Occupancy (C of O) and how long does it grant?
answer_or_content: A Certificate of Occupancy (C of O) is a statutory document issued by a state government under the Land Use Act of 1978 granting an individual, company, or institution the legal right to occupy and use a specific parcel of land, typically for 99 years. Because all land is technically vested in the state governor under the Act, a C of O is the primary legal proof of land ownership in Nigeria and protects against disputes.

question_or_title: What are the general steps to obtain a Certificate of Occupancy?
answer_or_content: Generally: 1) Commission a registered surveyor to prepare a survey plan of the land. 2) Submit an application to the state land bureau/ministry with evidence of land ownership or purchase, the completed application form, and required fees. 3) Obtain Governor's Consent, which validates the transfer of ownership. 4) Pay stamp duty and registration fees. 5) The Governor signs and the C of O is issued upon approval.

question_or_title: How much does a Certificate of Occupancy cost in Lagos State?
answer_or_content: Costs vary by land size and location, but for residential land in Lagos, C of O fees (including survey, processing, and issuance fees) commonly range from roughly ₦100,000 to ₦300,000 or more, excluding legal fees. Separately, overall property registration/transfer costs (consent fees, stamp duty, registration) typically add about 4%–8% of the purchase price in Lagos as of 2026.

question_or_title: How long does it take to get a Certificate of Occupancy?
answer_or_content: Processing time varies significantly by state and the efficiency of the local land registry, generally ranging from three months to as long as two years.

question_or_title: Can I get a bank loan using land without a Certificate of Occupancy?
answer_or_content: No. Nigerian banks and financial institutions generally require a valid Certificate of Occupancy before they will accept land as viable collateral for a loan.

question_or_title: What replaced Nigeria's old NHIS and what does it cover?
answer_or_content: The National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA), established under the NHIA Act of 2022, replaced the former National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS). It runs several programmes: Formal Sector Social Health Insurance (for government/private employees), GIFSHIP (Group, Individual and Family Social Health Insurance for the self-employed/informal sector), TISHIP (for tertiary students), and coverage for vulnerable groups such as pregnant women, children, the elderly, and persons with disabilities.

question_or_title: Is health insurance mandatory for employers in Nigeria?
answer_or_content: Yes, for larger employers. Under Sections 3 and 14 of the NHIA Act, employers with five or more staff are legally required to enrol those employees in an NHIA-approved health insurance plan. In September 2025, the President directed all federal Ministries, Departments, and Agencies to enrol their employees, and the House of Representatives has directed NHIA to compile and sanction defaulting private companies.

question_or_title: How do self-employed Nigerians register for NHIA coverage under GIFSHIP?
answer_or_content: Self-employed/informal-sector Nigerians register under GIFSHIP by visiting any NHIA office (or the official online portal), filling the enrolment form, paying the applicable premium (individual, couple, or family plan), and providing their NIN. An NHIA ID is issued within a few days, and enrolees can choose their preferred Health Maintenance Organization (HMO) and Health Care Provider.

question_or_title: How much does individual/family GIFSHIP enrolment cost?
answer_or_content: As individual enrolment, one person pays roughly ₦22,000 annually (with the option to add up to two more people at ₦22,000 each, i.e., ₦66,000 for three). Family enrolment ranges from ₦66,000 up to a maximum of ₦198,000 annually depending on family size (4–9 members). A separate NHIA ID card fee of ₦1,500 applies per enrolee. Groups of 10 pay a minimum of ₦220,000 annually, with each additional person costing ₦22,000.

question_or_title: How are contributions split for the Formal Sector Social Health Insurance Programme (FSHIP)?
answer_or_content: Under FSHIP (public and private sector employees), the employer contributes 10% and the employee contributes 5% of salary toward NHIA health insurance premiums.

question_or_title: What is CERPAC and who needs it?
answer_or_content: The Combined Expatriate Residence Permit and Aliens Card (CERPAC) is a residence permit and identity document issued by the Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) to foreign nationals residing or working in Nigeria. It is mandatory for any non-Nigerian intending to stay in the country beyond 56 consecutive days for employment, business, or long-term residence.

question_or_title: How much does a CERPAC cost and how long is it valid?
answer_or_content: The standard government fee is US$2,000 per year for employed foreigners (a rate unchanged since December 2018, when it was doubled from $1,000). Students pay US$600, and foreigners married to Nigerian citizens are exempt (gratis). CERPAC is typically issued for one year and renewable, with some categories valid up to two years (requiring $4,000 upfront if paid for two years at once).

question_or_title: What is the general process to obtain a CERPAC?
answer_or_content: 1) Submit an online application through the NIS e-CERPAC portal. 2) Upload required documents: valid passport with Nigerian visa, proof of employment/business registration/student status, and other supporting documents. 3) Pay the applicable fee online. 4) Provide biometric data (fingerprints and photograph) at a designated NIS office. 5) NIS processes and verifies the application before issuing the card.

question_or_title: What is the e-CERPAC and how is it different from the older process?
answer_or_content: The e-CERPAC is an electronic version that eliminates the need for post-arrival regularisation: it is processed and issued before the expatriate even enters Nigeria, streamlining what was previously a post-arrival application process and reducing administrative delays.

question_or_title: Does an employer need an Expatriate Quota before hiring a foreign worker?
answer_or_content: Yes. The employer must first have an approved Expatriate Quota authorizing the company to employ a specific number of foreign nationals in specific approved roles. Only after securing the quota can the employer sponsor the foreign candidate's Subject to Regularisation (STR) visa, after which the employee enters Nigeria and applies for CERPAC to gain legal residence and work authorization.

question_or_title: When did 2026 JAMB UTME registration open and how much does it cost?
answer_or_content: 2026 UTME registration ran from 20 January to 3 March 2026. Registration fees vary depending on whether a candidate opts for the optional mock exam, which costs an additional ₦1,500; JAMB reported no fee hikes for the 2026 cycle compared to the prior year.

question_or_title: How do I check my 2026 JAMB UTME result by SMS?
answer_or_content: Send a message containing 'UTME RESULT' or 'UTMERESULT' (in capital letters, no spacing) from the exact phone number used during registration to the shortcode 55019 or 66019. A charge of ₦50–₦100 (varies by report) is deducted from your airtime, and you receive an SMS reply with your score. Using a different phone number than the one registered will return an error message.

question_or_title: How do I check my JAMB result online and print an official result slip?
answer_or_content: Sign in to your JAMB e-Facility account using your registered email/username and password, navigate to the result-checking area, and select 'Print Result Slip.' Printing the original result slip (which includes your biometric passport photo, institutional preferences, and a security barcode) attracts a ₦500 fee payable via ATM card or other options on JAMB CAPS.

question_or_title: How many candidates registered for the 2026 UTME and how quickly were results released?
answer_or_content: The 2026 UTME, conducted 16–23 April 2026, attracted 2,243,816 registered candidates — a 10.5% increase over the roughly 2.03 million who registered in 2025. Over 1.9 million results were processed and released within 48 hours of the final paper, released in rolling batches by exam date.

question_or_title: Is UTME mandatory for admission into all Nigerian tertiary institutions?
answer_or_content: For admission into most traditional Nigerian universities, yes — UTME is required. However, some accredited alternatives exist; for example, certain licensed open/flexible universities admit students directly with a minimum of five O'Level credits (WAEC, NECO, GCE, or NABTEB) including English and Mathematics in no more than two sittings, without requiring UTME.

question_or_title: Is a BVN now mandatory to register or update a Retirement Savings Account (RSA)?
answer_or_content: Yes. A PenCom circular effective 1 February 2025 made the 11-digit Bank Verification Number (BVN) mandatory for all new Retirement Savings Account (RSA) registrations and for data recapture updates to existing RSA records. Pension Fund Administrators (PFAs) must mark the BVN field as mandatory on their registration and data recapture forms.

question_or_title: What documents does PenCom require to register an RSA for a formal-sector employee?
answer_or_content: Requirements include a Letter of Employment/Appointment and a means of identification — acceptable options include a Staff Identity Card, International Passport, or a National Identity Card/Enrolment Slip issued by NIMC showing the NIN. If a Staff ID Card is provided, additional ID requirements may be waived; the BVN is mandatory in all cases as of February 2025.

question_or_title: What is PenCom's data recapture self-service platform launched in 2026?
answer_or_content: From 1 February 2026, PenCom's self-service platform allows eligible Retirement Savings Account holders to update their biodata and biometric information directly online, as part of an ongoing Data Recapture Exercise (first launched in 2019) that uses the Enhanced Contributor Registration System integrated with NIMC to verify identities and harmonise RSA records with national identity data.

question_or_title: How do I get a Bank Verification Number (BVN) in Nigeria?
answer_or_content: BVN registration requires in-person enrolment — you cannot get a BVN entirely online. If residing in Nigeria, visit your bank branch to have your biometrics (fingerprints and photo) captured and linked to your BVN. Nigerians abroad can use partner enrolment centres (operated in partnership with the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System, NIBSS) in select countries, typically by appointment.

question_or_title: What is the BVN and when was it introduced?
answer_or_content: The Bank Verification Number (BVN) is an 11-digit unique identifier assigned to each individual across the Nigerian banking industry, launched by the Central Bank of Nigeria in collaboration with all banks on 14 February 2014. It strengthens banking security, reduces financial fraud, and streamlines identity verification and authentication across banking transactions.

question_or_title: What is a Police Character Certificate and how do I apply?
answer_or_content: A Police Character Certificate (also called a Police Clearance Certificate) is an official document issued by the Nigeria Police Force confirming whether an individual has a criminal record; it's commonly required for visa processing, study/employment abroad, and background checks. Applications are made through the Police Specialised Services Automation Project (POSSAP) portal at possap.gov.ng: applicants complete most of the process online (personal details, ID type — NIN, BVN, or International Passport — and a recent passport photo), then visit a designated police command or formation in person for biometric capture.

question_or_title: How long does a Nigerian Police Character Certificate take and how long is it valid?
answer_or_content: Once biometrics are captured, standard processing takes about 3 to 7 working days, after which a digital, verifiable PDF copy is emailed and can be downloaded anytime from the applicant's POSSAP account. The certificate is generally valid for three months (90 days) from its date of issue.

question_or_title: Can Nigerians abroad apply for a Police Character Certificate without returning home?
answer_or_content: Yes. Nigerians living abroad can begin the application online via POSSAP using their NIN or BVN. However, biometric fingerprint capture generally cannot be done by proxy — a trusted contact in Nigeria can submit supporting documents at Force CID on the applicant's behalf, but the applicant's own fingerprints must eventually be captured, either during a visit to Nigeria or through an accepted alternative arrangement, which can extend processing to several weeks or months.

question_or_title: Is registering for NIN free?
answer_or_content: Yes, NIN enrolment itself is free of charge at NIMC and designated ward-level enrolment centres. Costs only arise for ancillary services such as replacement of a lost NIN slip/card, premium/expedited services, or third-party printing — official first-time enrolment carries no fee.

question_or_title: What biometric data does NIMC capture during NIN enrolment?
answer_or_content: NIMC captures all ten fingerprints, a facial photograph, and a signature during in-person enrolment at an approved centre, alongside demographic data (name, date of birth, address, etc.) either entered by an enrolment officer or auto-populated by scanning a pre-enrolment barcode slip.

question_or_title: What is the minimum CAC fee to register an Incorporated Trustee (NGO/church/association)?
answer_or_content: Registering Incorporated Trustees (used for NGOs, churches, foundations, and associations) with the CAC involves a set of incorporation forms, separate from company or business name fees, with published fees for the initial forms and additional charges of ₦100 for each extra form, per CAC's official fee schedule.

question_or_title: Do I need to renew or re-register my CAC business name periodically?
answer_or_content: You do not re-register from scratch, but every CAC-registered entity (business name or company) must file annual returns each year to remain in 'Active' status; failure to file attracts an escalating monthly penalty, and prolonged non-compliance can result in the name being struck off the register.

question_or_title: What happens if I lose my Nigerian passport — how much does replacement cost?
answer_or_content: A lost passport is replaced at the same fee as a fresh 64-page passport application within Nigeria (₦200,000) — there is no discount for loss, and applicants are generally advised to file a police report and follow the standard fresh-application process through the NIS portal.

question_or_title: What is the general process to register a new vehicle in Nigeria?
answer_or_content: After purchase, obtain proof of ownership documents, then visit the state vehicle licensing office to complete an Allocation of Plate Number Form. Pay the required fees (number plate fee, vehicle licence fee, roadworthiness certificate fee, registration fee, and insurance), after which the licensing authority issues proof of ownership documents. FRSC then assigns and issues the physical number plate, which must be correctly attached, along with a Vehicle Identification Tag (VIT).

question_or_title: How much does vehicle registration cost in Lagos?
answer_or_content: Combined registration fees (number plate, vehicle licence, roadworthiness certificate, registration, and insurance) typically range from roughly ₦30,000 to ₦50,000, varying by vehicle type and state.

question_or_title: How do I verify if a used ('tokunbo') car's registration and customs duty are legitimate before buying?
answer_or_content: You can dial the USSD code *7031# to instantly confirm whether the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) is registered on the national VREG system and whether Customs Duty has been fully paid. Separately, verify the number plate on the National Vehicle Identification System (NVIS) to confirm it is legally assigned to that specific vehicle, and check for a 'recycling tag' confirming the mandatory recycling fee has been settled under 2026 rules.

question_or_title: What government portal manages Nigeria's national vehicle registry?
answer_or_content: VREG (Vehicle Registration System, vreg.gov.ng) is the national platform for vehicle registration services, including VIN registration by importers, VIN verification/registration status checks, and processing requests to transfer vehicle ownership from one person to another.

question_or_title: What does a vehicle roadworthiness certificate confirm and how is compliance tracked?
answer_or_content: A roadworthiness certificate confirms a vehicle passed a physical inspection assessing its fitness for road use; the certificate is affixed to the vehicle. A validity tag or e-Tag is also pasted on the windscreen so officials can quickly confirm current roadworthiness status during routine road checks without needing the physical certificate on hand.

question_or_title: What are the two types of registry ('court') marriages recognized in Nigeria and how long is the notice period?
answer_or_content: Nigeria's Marriage Act recognizes an Ordinary Marriage (between two Nigerians), which requires a 21-day public notice period, and a Special Marriage (between a Nigerian and a non-Nigerian, or between two non-Nigerians), which requires a shorter 7-day notice period. In both cases, a Letter/Notice of Marriage Intention is displayed at the registry for public inspection before the marriage can proceed.

question_or_title: What core documents are needed for a Nigerian court/registry marriage?
answer_or_content: Both parties generally need: a Birth Certificate or Declaration of Age, passport photographs, a valid government-issued ID (NIN slip/card, international passport, driver's licence, or voter's card), and a Sworn Affidavit of Bachelorhood/Spinsterhood from a law court. Additional documents are required for special circumstances — e.g., decree nisi/absolute for divorcees, a deceased spouse's death certificate for widows/widowers, or a parental consent letter if either party is under 21.

question_or_title: What is the minimum legal age to marry under Nigeria's Marriage Act?
answer_or_content: Both parties must generally be of marriageable age, which is 18 years in most states; consent of both parties (and of parents/guardians if either party is under 21) is also required.

question_or_title: Can a Nigerian be validly married under the Marriage Act if already married under customary law?
answer_or_content: No. Under Section 33(1) of the Marriage Act, a statutory marriage is invalid if either party is, at the time of the ceremony, already married under customary/native law to another person whose marriage has not been legally dissolved. A registrar must be satisfied there is no subsisting marriage of any kind before issuing a certificate to marry.
